predecessors.name: Duchy of Legnica
predecessors.text: the northern Głogów territory that Konrad I received from his elder brother Bolesław II the Bald of Legnica in 1251

successors.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
successors.text: the Bohemian shape of 1314, which covers Głogów (5 of the 6 cells around the town)

ledger.x: 1251: Konrad I founds the lasting Duchy of Głogów.
1279: Cliopatria hands the Lubusz and Żagań cells to its Duchy of Silesia shape.
July 1290: Henry III goes to war for the Duchy of Wrocław.
November 1293: Henry III takes Henry V the Fat prisoner and the war for Wrocław ends.
1294: Henry V buys his freedom with towns.
1296: Głogów expands to the east and south-west.
March 1297: Henry III renounces Bolesławiec and Chojnów.
1306: Henry III advances into Greater Poland.
1309: the end of Henry III's tenure as Duke of Greater Poland.
1312: Oleśnica and Wołów are split off.
ledger.cp: Duchies of Oleśnica and Wołów (Henry III's sons)

ledger.x: 1313: the last Cliopatria shape of the Duchy of Głogów.

wars.name: Battle of Stolec (1277)
wars.outcome: The coalition of Henry III and Ottokar II was 'defeated in the Battle of Stolec on 24 April 1277' (Henry III page).

wars.name: War for the Duchy of Wrocław (Henry III of Głogów against Henry V the Fat of Legnica)
wars.outcome: Henry III declared war in July 1290 after the Wrocław rebels invited Henry V; Henry V was captured and paid a ransom of 30,000 pieces of silver in 1293, and Głogów gained towns in 1296.

wars.name: Henry III's war for Greater Poland
wars.outcome: After Wenceslaus II's death in 1305 Henry III advanced into Kuyavia and Gdańsk Pomerania (1306), took Kalisz (1307) and held parts of Greater Poland to 1309/1310; Władysław I conquered Greater Poland in 1314.

certainty.note: The duchy's frontiers are lists of towns and castellanies, not surveyed lines; the page gives no treaty boundary.
